info.title: TryggHverdag API
info.description: The server that watches journeys home. Every route lives under /v1; a breaking change gets a new version rather than changing this one, because phones keep running old app versions (AR-08).

deviceCredential.description: The device’s own credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The server keeps only its hash.

get.description: Returns 200 whenever the API is up. Read `status` in the body to tell whether the worker is still running, because an API with no worker raises no alerts.

status.description: ok when the worker has checked in recently; degraded when it has not, which means nothing is watching the journeys.

checkedAt.description: When the server answered, from the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

lastBeatAt.description: The worker’s last check-in, or null if it has never checked in.

silentForMs.description: How long the worker has been silent, or null if it has never checked in.

worker.description: What the API can see of the worker.

schema.description: Whether the safety system as a whole is working, not just this process.

post.description: Needs a device credential: the walker is the user whose device sends it. A walker can have only one unended journey, so a second start is refused with 409 and the ID of the journey already running.

responderIds.description: The users who should follow this journey. Each must be a member of the walker's group other than the walker; a repeated ID counts once. An empty list is accepted here and refused as NO_RESPONDER.

schema.description: A start request. The walker is the user whose device sends it; no field names one.

startedAt.description: When the journey started, from the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

schema.description: The journey that started.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
The walker already has a journey that has not ended.
A responder named is the walker, or is not a member of the walker's group.
A journey needs at least one responder to start.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Answers only for the device user’s own journeys, and only from the device that started the journey. A 200, RECORDED or DUPLICATE, means the server has the event, so the phone may drop it. A 409 means the journey has ended: stop sending.

journeyId.description: The journey this heartbeat belongs to.

eventId.description: The heartbeat’s own ID, unique within its journey. Sent again, it changes nothing and is answered DUPLICATE (SM-08).

batteryLevel.description: The battery level from 0 to 1, or null when the phone does not know it.

accuracyMeters.description: The position’s accuracy in metres, 0 or more.

recordedAt.description: When the phone recorded the position, by the phone’s clock, as RFC 3339 with an offset, whose instant in UTC falls in the years 0001 to 9999. Within those years, any time is accepted, however far from the server’s clock: it labels the position and decides nothing (REL-01).

anyOf.description: Where the phone was, as the phone recorded it.

position.description: The position, or null when the phone has none (SM-03).

schema.description: A heartbeat. The walker is the user whose device sends it, and the device must be the one that started the journey; no field names either.

200.description: The server has the heartbeat, so the phone may drop it.

outcome.description: RECORDED when the heartbeat was stored now; DUPLICATE when its journey already had its event ID, so nothing changed.

schema.description: The server has the heartbeat, so the phone may drop it.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
Only the device that started this journey can send its heartbeats.
The walker has no journey with this ID.
The journey has ended, so the heartbeat was not stored. Stop sending them.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Ends the journey named in the path; only the device that started the journey may end it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, ENDED, and a 409, JOURNEY_ENDED, both mean the journey is over: stop tracking it and drop anything queued for it.

schema.description: The journey to end.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.
The journey is over, so the phone may stop tracking it.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
Only the device that started this journey can end it.
The walker has no journey with this ID.
The journey has already ended.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Says "I’m on it" for the alert named in the path; only a responder of the alert’s journey may acknowledge it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, ACKNOWLEDGED, means the caller is the one on it, recorded now or already. A 409, ALREADY_ACKNOWLEDGED, means another responder is on it; a 409, ALERT_RESOLVED, means the alert is over.

schema.description: The alert to acknowledge.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

outcome.description: The caller is the one on this alert.

schema.description: The caller is on it: recorded now, or already theirs.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
The caller follows no alert with this ID.
Another responder is already on this alert.
The alert is over.

post.description: Needs a device credential. Closes the alert named in the path once the walker is known to be safe; only the responder on the alert may close it. The body is empty, or absent. A 200, CLOSED, means the alert is resolved and the journey has ended, and the other responders are told. A 403, NOT_THE_ACKNOWLEDGER, means the caller is not the one on it; a 409, ALERT_RESOLVED, means the alert is over.

schema.description: The alert to close.
Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

outcome.description: The alert is closed, and its journey has ended.

schema.description: Closed now: the walker is safe, and the other responders are told.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
Only the responder on this alert can close it.
The caller follows no alert with this ID.
The alert is over.

post.summary: Join the group with an invitation
post.description: Public: needs no device credential. Joins the group with an invitation code, or, while no group exists, as its first admin with the bootstrap code. The answer carries the device credential once, and is not cached. The same code sent again with the same join key, while the invitation has not expired and its member has not been removed, is the same join retried: the same member, and a new credential that replaces the first. A 404, INVITATION_NOT_VALID, is the one answer for every code that lets nobody in.

invitationCode.description: The invitation code as typed: 20 base32 characters, in any case, with spaces or hyphens between, O read as 0 and I or L as 1. The first admin types the bootstrap code here.

joinKey.description: A key the phone makes once, 32 random bytes as base64url, and sends again with a retried join, so a join whose answer was lost can be retried.

displayName.description: The name the person typed for themself: 1 to 40 characters once the spaces around it are trimmed; no control character; no bidirectional control or other format character but ZWNJ (U+200C) and ZWJ (U+200D); and at least one visible character.

schema.description: A join: the code, the phone’s join key, and the name the person typed.

credential.description: This phone’s device credential, shown once: keep it in secure storage, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.

userId.description: The member this phone is signed in as.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

schema.description: Joined: a member of the group, signed in on this phone.

message.default: Input validation failed
The invitation is not valid. Ask the admin for a new one.

get.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Lists every member: their ID, the name they typed and their role.

displayName.description: The name the member typed when they joined.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

schema.description: The members of the group.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.

get.summary: Who this phone is signed in as
get.description: Needs a device credential. Answers the member the device belongs to: their ID, the name they typed and their role. A 401 means this phone is no longer signed in to the group.

200.description: The member this phone is signed in as.

displayName.description: The name the member typed when they joined.

role.description: ADMIN for the one admin; MEMBER for everyone else.

schema.description: A member of the group.

message.default: A valid device credential is required.
This device belongs to no member of the group.

post.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Makes an invitation that brings one person in, once, within seven days. Only its hash is kept, so the code is shown once.

schema.description: Nothing: an empty object, or no body at all.

invitationCode.description: The code, shown once: 20 base32 characters in four groups of five.

expiresAt.description: When it expires: seven days after it was made, by the database clock (REL-01), as RFC 3339.

schema.description: A new invitation: it brings one person in, once, before it expires.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.

delete.summary: Remove a member from the group
delete.description: Needs the admin’s device credential. Removes the member at once, in one step: their phones are signed out, they are taken off every journey they follow that has not ended, and nothing more is sent to them. A journey of their own that has not ended runs to its end. A 404, MEMBER_NOT_FOUND, after a removal whose answer was lost means it is done.

schema.description: The member to remove.
Removed, all of it, now.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
Only the admin can do this.
The group has no member with this ID.
The admin cannot be removed.

delete.summary: Remove a responder from a journey
delete.description: Needs the walker’s device credential. Removes the responder named in the path from the walker’s journey named in the path: anything not yet sent to them about it is withdrawn, an alert they were on goes back to unacknowledged, and when none is left the walker is warned. A 409, NOT_A_RESPONDER, after a removal whose answer was lost means it is done.

schema.description: The walker’s journey.
The responder to remove from it.
Removed: they follow the journey no more, and nothing more is sent to them about it.

message.default: Input validation failed
A valid device credential is required.
The walker has no journey with this ID.
The user named is not a responder of this journey.
The journey has already ended.
